Find out why five automated runs of JusPrin's test app fail on the development branch, and fix each one.

## Background

JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer at /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin. Read AGENTS.md first, then tests/AGENTS.md. The development branch is `jusprin-dev`; the main checkout holds it, so never check `jusprin-dev` out in a worktree. Work in your own worktree under /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/, on a new branch cut from the current head of `jusprin-dev`.

The test app is the shell harness: source `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`, build target `shell_integration_harness`, run as
`build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --<mode>`.
It drives the real app through about forty automated modes and prints one line per check: `HARNESS CHECK <name> PASS` or `FAIL`. It uses its own data folder. Never drive Kenneth's own running JusPrin.

On 2026-11-16 another session ran every automated mode. Five fail, and they failed the same way before that session's work, so the causes are older and nobody has looked for them. They were last seen failing on `jusprin-dev` at commit 3c134d39e3.

## The failures

Counts are the number of failing checks. Some counts moved by one between runs, so treat the names as examples and the first run as your own baseline.

- `--print-issues`: 6 to 7 checks, about a reply that is still running. Example: `buttons_are_disabled_while_a_reply_is_running`.
- `--print-issue-readers`: 8 checks, about wording or printer-profile differences from OrcaSlicer. Example: `a4_toolpath_outside_in_orcas_words`.
- `--printer-network-check`: 1 to 2 checks. Example: `first_read_tool_called`.
- `--printer-connect-skill`: 3 checks. Example: `connect_skill_printer_added`.
- `--project-prompt-requests`: 1 to 3 checks, varying with machine load. Example: `print-hook-plan-slice_answer_printer_list_has_its_result`.

Two more things were seen and not explained. Note them only if you see them yourself:
- `--printer-chat-sheet` passes every check but crashed once on exit (exit code 139) in about 15 runs, on `jusprin-dev` both with and without the latest commit.
- `--chat-restoration` crashed once on exit in more than 35 runs.

## What to do

1. Build first. Several sessions share this Mac: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` before building, pass `-- -j4`, run one build per build directory, and never restart a running build to change targets. Reuse the dependencies at /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64 and configure with BUILD_TESTS=ON.
2. Run each of the five modes on your branch, one at a time, and record exactly which checks fail. Run each failing mode at least three times, so you know which failures are steady and which come and go.
3. For each failing check, decide which is wrong: the app or the check. Use `git log -S` and `git blame` to find the commit that changed the behaviour or the check, and name it.
   - If the app is wrong, fix the app. Show the check failing before and passing after.
   - If the check is stale, change it to what the app is meant to do, and name the commit that made it stale.
   - If the failure depends on timing or load, say so with numbers (how many runs, how many failures) and fix the wait itself. Do not just raise a timeout.
4. Never apply a fix for a failure you have not reproduced. List anything you could not reproduce and leave it alone.
5. Follow the Error handling section of AGENTS.md in any app code you touch: no new catch, default or sentence for a failure the person cannot act on.

## Done looks like

- Each of the five modes exits 0 on your branch, three runs in a row.
- One commit per cause, with the reason in the message. No attribution lines in commit messages.
- These still pass: `build/arm64/tests/agent/Release/agent_bridge_tests.app/Contents/MacOS/agent_bridge_tests`, `build/arm64/tests/jusprin/Release/jusprin_tests.app/Contents/MacOS/jusprin_tests`, and the harness's default run.
- `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh` passes on your changed lines.
- Commit on your own branch only. Do not push, and do not touch `jusprin-dev`.

## Report

Open with two or three sentences a reader who has not seen this prompt can follow. Then give one line per failing check: what was wrong, the commit that caused it, and what you changed. End with what you could not reproduce, and the full path of your worktree and the name of your branch.

# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

Added 2026-11-01 in ff2fee4fbd on claude/festive-lederberg-693438 (unmerged). `printer_connect` and `printer_connection_status` have only `ToolExposure::Printer`, so MCP answers "This tool is not exposed by JusPrin MCP", despite what [[manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe]] implies for "any tool".

`JusPrinShellHarness --printer-network-check <dir> <address> <plugin-version> [--simulate-announce]`: copy `plugins/` from the real data folder into `<dir>` first. Without the flag it needs a P1S in cloud mode on; with it, the harness replays the logged announcement into `DeviceManager::on_machine_alive` at 25 s, which tests everything after the plug-in.

Another running JusPrin holding UDP 2021 hides the printer (2026-11-01, same P1S: nothing in 120 s with it running, found in 8 s with it quit), so quit it first (`lsof -nP -iUDP:2021`). Bambu Studio and OrcaSlicer not tried.

The plug-in's `start_discovery` returns success even when the port is held, and it binds UDP 2021 only as the app starts: after the holder lets go, stop + start (with waits, with the sending flag) and `hot_reload_network_plugin()` all left the port empty on 2026-11-01. So the app reports `port_taken` / `not_listening` and asks for a restart; do not retry a recovery without a new idea. Hold the port from a Python socket to test those states.

Port 8883 timing out while the printer announces on UDP (seen 2026-11-01 07:30) is not noise: hearing a printer says nothing about whether it can be logged in to. I wrote this off at the time as "no test of whether a P1S is on", and that same fault then hid behind the "refused" note, see [[bambu-code-minus-one-not-wrong-code]]. To test whether it is on, bind UDP 2021 and listen. To test whether it can be connected, check port 8883 too.

A harness PASS that only checks a note appeared says nothing about whether the note is true. On 2026-11-01 I quoted "in LAN mode, which can be connected" as proof, though only an announcement had been heard.

LAN mode, 2026-11-01: on the same P1S, LAN Only changes the announcement to `DevConnect: lan`, `DevBind: free`. The committed check fails there because it expects cloud mode; those runs used a temporary script. Whether a run starts before the printer is heard depends on the announcement timing (about every 20 s), so check the first "heard" line. A status read that lists the printer suppresses the note by design, so leave it out when testing the note.

Wrong access code, 2026-11-02, P1S firmware 01.10.00.00 in LAN mode, plug-in 02.03.00.62: a connection with a wrong 8-character code made the plug-in answer `ConnectStatusFailed` with msg `-1`, twice, not the `5` upstream's handler treats as a wrong password. So the erase did not run and the wrong code stayed saved. Whether `-1` means the printer refused the code is not known: the plug-in's own log is encrypted (`debug_network_*.log.enc`), TCP 8883 and 990 did accept connections from the same Mac, and a run with the real code has not been done to compare. `5` has never been seen on real hardware.

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

# JusPrin's translations

JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for
(`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's
catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own
text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never
conflicts in a translation file:

| Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL`, `translated_plural` | `native/<lang>.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`, the catalog the app loads |
| The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/<lang>.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) |

Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of
`native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used.

## Updating the catalogs

After marking or changing text:

```bash
python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py
```

It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the
pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new
entry in every `<lang>.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's
`AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line
break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine
translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: <what>` where
the meaning or the wording is uncertain. `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails
while any entry is untranslated or a translation loses a placeholder.

The page catalogs use ICU placeholders: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags like
`<0>…</0>` for elements inside a `Trans`, and
`{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` for counts. Keep the
placeholder and tag names; translate the words, including the words inside a
plural's branches, and give the plural the categories the language uses
(`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`).

## Marking text

Mark every string a person reads: labels, buttons, headings, menu items,
tooltips, `aria-label`s, placeholders, empty states, confirmation and error
text. Do not change the English: marking must leave the source text exactly
as it was.

Leave these in English, unmarked:

- **Text the AI model reads**: prompts, skills, tool descriptions and tool
  results, the project and printer instructions, anything that goes into a
  request to a model. The model speaks the person's language on its own, and
  `wording.test.ts` guards that text. When the same string is shown to the
  person and also sent to the model, translate it only where it is shown.
- Identifiers and values the code compares, protocol fields, CSS classes,
  test ids, file names, URLs, setting keys, G-code.
- Log lines and the text of error reports (`report_unexpected`,
  `report_error`): they are read by developers.
- Names: JusPrin, OrcaSlicer, Bambu Lab, printer and filament model names.

The harness fix 084b8d35a7 gave the default run a placeholder key for this reason, but not these modes. I'll confirm it with a temporary print on my own build before changing anything.
- **`--print-issue-readers`:** the checks are stale. The OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 merge (975c703f08) brought in three upstream changes the scenario predates:

  - A prime tower partly off the plate now blocks slicing instead of only warning (upstream 81357695c5).
  - Upstream reworded one sentence to "A G-code path goes beyond plate boundaries." (upstream 514ab02525c). JusPrin's copy in `PrintIssueMonitor.cpp:519` still has the old wording. This one is an app fix.
- **`--project-prompt-requests`:** this depends on timing. When slicing is slow, the app answers the recorder's slice reads with "busy". On the third refusal it ends the model's turn, which is by design since f46e5ac05f. The recorder then sends one more read into a turn that has already ended, so that read never gets a result. The fix is to have the recorder stop reading once the app has ended the turn.
